conviction_note: Nothing material is unpriced. The CFO's 15 Sept NIM upgrade looks only partly in the Zacks NII bar ($12.63bn implies roughly a 2.41% NIM against his 2.42-2.43%, about $40-90m or under 1%). The FY NII arithmetic points to the ~$50bn guide being reaffirmed rather than raised, and this name sold its last three EPS beats on exactly that line. JPM and C report the same morning. So p_up is 50 and the expected move is 0, while abs_move stays at 4.5, between the 3.94% event-implied move and the 5.16% median reaction. The findings sum to -0.1, consistent with the scaled 0.
bar: Zacks consensus (TradingView/Zacks, ~2026-10-08): EPS $1.85, revenue $22.15bn, NII $12.63bn, noninterest income $9.58-9.59bn, IB fees $903.8m, avg earning assets $2,089.8bn, efficiency ratio 62.5%, NCOs $985.6m, CET1 10.1% (https://www.tradingview.com/news/zacks:8404cace6094b:0-wells-fargo-q3-earnings-on-the-deck-what-s-in-store-for-the-stock/ ; https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/wells-fargo-wfc-q3-earnings-121520212.html). Earnings Whispers has $1.84 and $22.22bn, and Visible Alpha has NII +5.5% y/y, roughly $12.6bn (https://seekingalpha.com/article/4953201-visible-alpha-breakdown-of-us-banks-q3-2026-earnings-expectations), so two sources agree. Company guide: FY26 NII ~$50bn ± (ex-markets ~$48bn, markets ~$2bn), FY expense ~$55.7bn, Q3 NIM down 1bp to flat (updated 2026-09-15 from down 3-4bp).
positioning_check: Short interest about 29.0M shares, ~0.96% of float. Days to cover 1.8 at the 2026-07-15 FINRA settlement (curvedtrading, https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/wfc/short-interest/) or 3.30 per Fintel (undated, https://fintel.io/ss/us/wfc). No September settlement found. Not crowded, so no squeeze mechanism. Baseline 25-delta skew is +1.0 vol point (balanced), put/call OI 0.63, event-implied move 3.94% (straddle 4.46%). Tape: run_up_5d +2.66%, run_up_20d -5.75%, 13.3% below the 52-week high. The stock fell 3% on the 2026-09-16 Fed hike and was down 8.4% from the hike by 09-24 against ~4% for XLF, then recovered from ~$80 on Oct 2 to $83.61 after a Morgan Stanley upgrade and a weak September jobs report (TIKR, last updated 2026-10-05).

findings.finding: On 2026-09-15 at Barclays the CFO said Q3 NIM would be 'maybe down 1, maybe flat' from Q2's 2.43%, against the 3-4bp decline management expected entering the quarter. Zacks consensus is NII $12.63bn on avg earning assets $2,089.8bn, which implies about 2.41% NIM after a ~1.5bp taxable-equivalent adjustment calibrated on Q3'25 (NII $11.95bn on AEA $1,832.5bn, reported 2.60%). At the CFO's 2.42-2.43% the same assets give NII of about $12.67-12.72bn, a $40-90m (0.3-0.7%) beat on the line this stock trades on.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last three prints were EPS beats sold on NII/NIM: 2026-01-14 -4.61%, 2026-04-14 -5.70% (Q1 NII $12.10bn, ~$200m below the $12.3bn bar), 2026-07-14 -2.71% (NII/NIM a touch light, guide held). 2025-10-14 rose +7.15%. The stock punishes NII misses and has not rewarded small NII beats in this sample.
findings.why_not_priced: The remark is public and was widely quoted (Bloomberg 2026-09-15), but the Zacks NII bar still implies ~2.41% NIM, i.e. about -2bp, between the old and the new guide. If the bar fully reflected it, consensus NII would sit near $12.7bn on the same earning-asset estimate. The stock fell 8% after the update because of the Fed hike, so the margin news never showed up in the price either.
findings.independence: TIKR 2026-09-30 quotes the same CFO line (https://www.tikr.com/blog/wells-fargo-stock-is-down-14-in-2026-time-to-sell-or-load-up). Same underlying remark, so not independent. The Q2 call (July) also said Q3 compression would be modest and 'maybe even better' (https://www.webull.com/news/15267023079547904).

findings.finding: The FY26 NII guide (~$50bn ±) looks likely to be reaffirmed, not raised. H1 NII was $24.41bn (1Q $12,096m + 2Q $12,317m, per the 2Q26 8-K), so H2 needs ~$25.59bn. A Q3 near $12.7bn plus a Q4 with stable NIM (CFO guide) and ~2% earning-asset growth (~$12.95bn) lands at about $50.0-50.1bn. The 16 Sept 25bp Fed hike helps the modestly asset-sensitive banking book only from late Q3. Against it, management says markets NII falls as rates rise, deposit costs rise modestly in H2, and non-interest-bearing deposits are only 'relatively stable'. The last two holds of this same guide were sold.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: April 2026 (guide held at ~$50bn after an NII miss) -5.70%. July 2026 (guide 'unchanged, not raised') -2.71%. The 2025-10-14 print (+7.15%) carried a raised ROTCE target rather than an NII change.
findings.why_not_priced: Previews quote '$50bn maintained' and NIM 'better than expected', which together read as a setup for a raise. The arithmetic says the better NIM is roughly what the $50bn already needed. If the market expected a plain reaffirmation, the stock would not have bounced 4% into the print on a 'NIM stabilise then improve' upgrade thesis (Morgan Stanley). It might be partly priced through the 11x NTM P/E de-rating.
findings.independence: The Barclays transcript (2026-09-15) confirms the ~$50bn hold incl. ~$2bn markets and 'markets NII lower as rates rise' (https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/wells-fargo-at-barclays-global-financial-services-conference-growth-broadens-93CH-4901834). The Q2 call confirms modestly rising deposit costs and stable NIB (https://www.webull.com/news/15267023079547904). Fed hike: Star-Advertiser 2026-09-17 (https://www.staradvertiser.com/2026/09/17/breaking-news/major-u-s-banks-raise-prime-rate-after-fed-rate-hike/). This finding and the NIM finding both rest partly on the CFO's Q3 NIM remark: the NIM finding is the Q3 print, this one is the FY guide.

findings.finding: Fed H.8 (2026-10-02 release, large domestically chartered banks, seasonally adjusted) shows industry loan growth slowing from ~7.5% annualised in Q2 to ~5.9% in Q3-to-date and deposits from ~8.2% to ~4.2%. That is a proxy for WFC's balance-sheet growth, which the CFO already said would slow from the H1 pace of ~12% y/y loans. Zacks' earning-asset bar ($2,089.8bn, ~+2.1% q/q or ~8.6% annualised) is ahead of the industry pace.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no clean history of reactions to earning-asset or loan-growth surprises alone. Loan growth beating guidance in H1 did not stop the NII-led selloffs.
findings.why_not_priced: Previews anchor on WFC's own 12% H1 loan growth and the CFO's 'beat original guidance' line, not on the industry series. If it were priced, the earning-asset bar would show deceleration nearer the industry's ~1.5% q/q.
findings.independence: This is a proxy. The company itself said loan growth would slow from the H1 pace (https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/wells-fargo-at-barclays-global-financial-services-conference-growth-broadens-93CH-4901834), but WFC has outgrown the industry since the asset cap was lifted, so transmission is uncertain.

findings.finding: Fee lines sit at or inside guidance. The CFO guided Q3 IB fees up mid-single digits y/y and markets/trading up mid-single digits y/y, with venture gains 'roughly flat' after ~$850m in H1. Zacks has IB fees at $903.8m (+7.6% y/y, a touch above guide) and total noninterest income at $9.58bn, already down ~$0.7bn from Q2's $10.31bn, which absorbs the venture swing.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2's strong venture and IB fees produced a revenue beat that was still sold (-2.71%). Fee beats have not driven this stock's reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the bar sits on the guide. The only gap is IB consensus ~2-3 points above the CFO's mid-single-digit guide, worth about $20m.
findings.independence: Peer guidance diverged at the same conference: JPM IB and markets up mid-to-high teens, BofA IB down ≥10% with trading flat (https://pulse2.com/jpmorgan-expects-q3-investment-banking-fees-and-markets-revenue-to-rise-mid-to-high-teens/ ; https://theedgemalaysia.com/node/818142).

findings.finding: Morgan Stanley upgraded WFC from Equal-Weight to Overweight and named it a top pick ($102 PT) around early October, on the thesis that NIM stabilises then improves. WFC had been the worst performer in MS's coverage. The stock rose from ~$80 on Oct 2 to $83.61. Before that it had de-rated from ~14x to ~11x NTM P/E and fell 8.4% after the Sept 16 hike against ~4% for XLF.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Low-expectation entries have helped before: October 2025 +7.15% came after a period of scepticism. 2026 prints came off higher multiples and were sold.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced through the +2.66% 5-day run-up. What remains is that the multiple is already low (11x), so a held guide is less likely to be punished as hard as in April and July. If the bar were demanding, skew would be bid to the upside rather than balanced at +1.
findings.independence: TIKR 2026-09-30 documents the de-rating and the post-hike underperformance (https://www.tikr.com/blog/wells-fargo-stock-is-down-14-in-2026-time-to-sell-or-load-up). StreetInsider shows an average PT of $97.66 (https://www.streetinsider.com/rating_history.php?q=WFC).

findings.finding: JPMorgan (EPS bar ~$5.94) and Citigroup report Q3 2026 on the same morning, 2026-10-13, before the open, and BofA on Oct 14. WFC's reaction will be read against JPM's NII guide and IB/markets print, which JPM pre-guided up mid-to-high teens. That creates a sector cross-current of unknown sign within the window.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Big-bank prints cluster on the same day, and WFC's reactions (-2.71% to +7.15%) share that day's sector tape.
findings.why_not_priced: It is not directional: the timing is known and the sign is unknown. It is filed so judges can see that the window carries the peer read-through.
findings.independence: JPM's Oct 13 date: Zacks via search; JPM Barclays guide: https://pulse2.com/jpmorgan-expects-q3-investment-banking-fees-and-markets-revenue-to-rise-mid-to-high-teens/

findings.finding: Capital return capacity is visible but not in the bar. CET1 was 10.3% at Q2 against a 10-10.5% target. The CFO said buybacks run $3-6bn a quarter (Q2 was $3.0bn, 37.4m shares) and that proposed capital rules would cut RWA ~7%, though not before year-end. Zacks expects CET1 to fall to 10.1%, consistent with buybacks above $3bn or balance-sheet growth absorbing capital.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Buyback size has not been the line WFC traded on in 2026.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the range is public. A Q3 buyback toward $5-6bn would be the only surprise, and nothing seen indicates which end.
findings.independence: The Q2 release confirms $3.0bn of Q2 repurchases and CET1 of 10.3% (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000072971/000007297126000288/wfc2qer07-14x26ex991xrelea.htm). Zacks CET1 bar: https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/wells-fargo-wfc-q3-earnings-121520212.html

outside_window.finding: Finalisation of proposed capital rules (RWA down ~7% per the CFO) would free buyback capacity. The CFO said it is unlikely before year-end.
The 2027 NII and expense outlook is normally given with Q4 results on 2027-01-14. The CFO gave no 2027 numbers in September.

baseline_tension: Nothing found cuts hard against the balanced skew (+1.0). The modest NII-beat lean agrees with the 5-day run-up and the MS upgrade, while the likely plain reaffirmation of the guide and three straight sold beats cut the other way. Net, the evidence is balanced.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction): this name sold its last three NII-line beats, so the NIM/NII-beat finding went from +0.5 to +0.3.
Rule 5 (macro proxy): the H.8 industry loan/deposit slowdown is a proxy the company has only partly confirmed, so it went from -0.3 to -0.2.
Rule 6 (verify the bar): the bar is sourced to Zacks plus Earnings Whispers/Visible Alpha and they agree, so no cap. The fee finding sits inside the CFO's guide and stays at -0.1.
Rule 7 (positioning): short interest is about 1% of float and skew is balanced, so the negative guidance finding was left at -0.5. p_up stays 50.
